recipes.name: Harness-in-sandbox call capture and trajectory replay
recipes.summary: Wrap the source system in the same agent harness the task is graded with, run it inside a disposable sandbox, and intercept the model boundary with a proxy so every call and every tool invocation is recorded. The recorded calls are reassembled into a prefix tree, which yields a replayable multi-turn trajectory and a state trace the verifier can compare against. Keeping the harness inside the sandbox and the policy outside it is what makes one procedure serve both grading a single Harbor task and collecting rollouts: the sandbox boundary is the isolation guarantee, the proxy is the observation point, and the prefix tree is the artifact that names the intermediate states a correct solution has to pass through.
when_to_use: the source is an agent harness, a multi-tool app or a service with side effects
the task must be checked on intermediate tool-call state, not only on the final artifact
each attempt needs its own isolated environment instance
not_when_to_use: the task is a single deterministic command with a file-level answer
no proxy or harness layer can be inserted between the model and the tools
inputs: the source system or repository plus a runnable harness that drives it
a disposable sandbox substrate whose files and processes survive between turns
a proxy endpoint placed between the model and the harness

steps.title: Stand up a disposable sandbox per attempt
steps.detail: Each task instance gets its own temporary sandbox holding the source checkout, its dependencies and its starting files, and the harness runs inside it so no state leaks between attempts. Keep harness and task environment inside the same sandbox boundary instead of splitting them across hosts.

steps.title: Insert a proxy at the model boundary
steps.detail: Route every model call through a local proxy that records request and response payloads verbatim. Policy decisions stay outside the sandbox while observation happens inside, so capture never changes the execution environment.

steps.title: Instrument tool execution separately
steps.detail: Have the harness log each tool call with its arguments, exit status and the stdout or stderr it produced. The tool log, not the model's narration, is the ground truth about what happened to the environment.

steps.title: Rebuild the multi-turn trajectory as a prefix tree
steps.detail: Group the captured calls by shared prefix so the trajectory branches wherever the agent could have diverged. The tree is the reconstruction of the multi-turn conversation and it makes the ordered sequence of intermediate states explicit.

steps.title: Extract the state checkpoints a correct run must hit
steps.detail: From the tool log, mark the points where the source system's observable state changed in a way the task depends on: a file written, a record moved to another status, a request accepted. These become the intermediate assertions, rather than checking only the final artifact.

steps.title: Pin the verifier to the state trace
steps.detail: Write the checker against the recorded state transitions plus the final artifact, so a run that reaches the same end state through an illegal path still fails.

steps.title: Re-run in a fresh sandbox to confirm reproducibility
steps.detail: Rebuild the instance from scratch and replay the reference trajectory. An identical tool-call sequence and an identical final state digest must be reproduced; otherwise the environment has hidden state and the task will be flaky.

verifier: the reference run's tool-call sequence and final state digest are reproduced identically on a fresh sandbox
named intermediate assertions hold at their checkpoints (a file exists with expected content, a record carries the expected status)
every recorded tool call carries an exit status equal to the reference
no two task instances share a sandbox or a mutable path
pitfalls: a proxy that rewrites requests silently breaks consistency between capture and grading
reconstructing the trajectory from the model's messages alone loses tool output and no longer matches what ran
state living outside the sandbox, such as host paths or shared caches, makes the environment non-reproducible

recipes.name: Simulated API/UI environment with internal state validation
recipes.summary: Model the source system as a simulator: tools and UI endpoints are re-implemented over an explicit internal state store, and every response is derived from that store instead of being improvised. Two properties make the result usable as a Harbor task. The simulator validates its own internal state after every transition, so inconsistent or reward-hacking trajectories are rejected rather than rewarded, and faults are injected in controlled proportions, which lets a task test whether the agent notices degraded data rather than whether it memorised a happy path. Instances are then filtered to the mid difficulty band where models neither pass trivially nor fail always.
when_to_use: the source is a web app, an admin UI or a service whose responses can be re-implemented
many task instances are needed over the same product surface
the check must read the state store rather than an LLM judge
not_when_to_use: the behaviour depends on live third-party services that cannot be re-implemented
the task requires pixel-exact rendering of the real interface
inputs: the source's API or UI specification plus a corpus of real requests and pages
an explicit state schema for the simulated domain
a fault-injection policy and agent rollouts used for difficulty calibration

steps.title: Extract the domain model first
steps.detail: Derive the entities, fields and transitions the source system exposes and write the state schema down before writing any endpoint, because the state store is what the verifier will read.

steps.title: Re-implement the tool and UI surface over that state
steps.detail: Each endpoint or screen action becomes a deterministic function of the state plus the request, and responses are rendered from the store rather than generated free-form.

steps.title: Keep an explicit, inspectable state store
steps.detail: Hold all state in a queryable database or file tree so a checker can read it directly and a simulated interaction can be replayed step by step.

steps.title: Validate internal state after every transition
steps.detail: After each action, run consistency checks over the store, covering referential integrity, required fields and legal state transitions, and reject the trajectory when they fail. This is what stops an agent from satisfying the goal by writing fields directly or by exploiting the simulator.

steps.title: Inject faults in controlled proportions
steps.detail: Schedule explicit errors such as timeouts and 5xx responses, implicit degradations such as truncated records and missing fields, and mixed cases. Keep the level such that the agent can recover but has to notice the degradation instead of trusting the response.

steps.title: Write tasks and checkers against the store
steps.detail: Express the goal as a predicate over final state, for example a row updated, a file written or an approval recorded, so the check is a query with a boolean answer rather than a rubric read by a model.

steps.title: Calibrate difficulty on the mid band
steps.detail: Run several agents on the instance and keep those whose historical pass rate sits around 30 to 70 percent. Instances that are always solved or always failed carry no ranking signal and only inflate cost.

steps.title: Confirm solvability and record the grading
steps.detail: Verify that a reference path exists for the instance before shipping it, and record which state predicates are checked so the grader is reproducible by a third party.

verifier: a final-state predicate is evaluated directly against the state store, for example a specific field equals a specific value
internal consistency checks pass at every transition of a valid trajectory
the fault schedule is fixed and reproducible, so the same instance injects the same faults on replay
a reference solution reaches the goal state from the pristine instance
pitfalls: responses generated by a model instead of computed from the state drift, and the checker no longer describes what the agent actually saw
fault injection that is too loud trains error avoidance instead of error detection
difficulty that comes from phrasing rather than from state is solved by capable models regardless of skill

source_papers.note: decouples environment creation from scalable execution, moves grading to verifiable execution outcomes, and mitigates reward hacking through rigorous internal state validation and testing
